HONG KONG (AP) — China’s passenger car exports jumped 73% year-on-year in May to around 809,000 vehicles, an industry group reported Wednesday, as higher gasoline and diesel prices due to the war in Iran raised interest in electric vehicles.

That’s up from about 796,000 passenger cars exported in April, data from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers showed.

Exports of new energy vehicles, including pure EVs and plug-in hybrids, more than doubled in May from a year earlier to about 435,000 passenger cars, or more than half the total.

Chinese automakers such as BYD have been stepping up their overseas expansions, targeting markets including in Latin America, Asia and Europe at a time when domestic demand is coming under pressure, partly due to scaled-back government incentives for drivers to switch to EVs.

Domestic passenger car sales in May fell 23.4% from a year earlier to 1.44 million vehicles, the CAAM said, the seventh straight month of year-on-year declines. Sales of cars with internal combustion engines — including gasoline and diesel vehicles — fell almost 42% from the year before as the share of EVs grew.

UBS bank expects China’s annual passenger car exports to rise about 40% in 2026 from a year earlier, with EV exports possibly up about 80%.

“The high oil price certainly has translated into further higher interest on the EV,” said Paul Gong, head of UBS’s China automotive industry research.

China’s car exports were stronger than expected in the first few months of this year, Gong said, while domestic car sales were weaker than expected.

Claire Yuan, an auto analyst at S&P Global Ratings, expects China’s passenger car exports to maintain strong momentum in 2026 and forecasts a year-on-year growth of 30% to 50%.

Roughly one in four new cars sold globally last year was electric, the International Energy Agency said in its latest annual global EV outlook, released in May, and that’s going to grow further this year despite a more sluggish start of the year.

EV sales could reach 23 million and make up nearly 30% of all cars sold in 2026, the IEA said.

China is the world’s largest producer of EVs, supplying the majority of EVs sold worldwide.

BYD, China’s largest EV maker, sold over 160,000 vehicles abroad in May, up 80% from the year before. It aims to sell 1.5 million vehicles overseas this year, up more than 40% from last year’s 1.05 million.

The automaker based in southern China overtook Tesla last year as the world’s biggest EV maker by sales.

Selling more cars overseas may also generate better profitability for Chinese carmakers, as an intense price war in China last year has eroded profitability for many automakers.

Yuan of S&P said China’s car sales could pick up in the second half of the year as buyers step up purchases after automakers launch fresh lineups.

MOON ALERT: There are no restrictions to shopping or important decisions today. The moon is in Aries.

ARIES (March 21-April 19)

This is a lovely day for you! The moon is in Aries dancing beautifully with lucky Jupiter and the sun. It is also lined up with gentle Neptune making you empathetic and tuned into your surroundings. You feel warm and friendly toward everyone, and are concerned for their welfare.

TAURUS (April 20-May 20)

A lot of Winnipeggers may shrug, but the end of Giant Tiger’s downtown store is a giant problem for many of the people living in the centre of the city.

It would have been difficult for anyone going into or passing by the Canadian discount chain’s Donald Street and Ellice Avenue location Thursday to miss the red notices posted on the store’s windows advising it will close on Nov. 7.

According to a 2024 Downtown Winnipeg BIZ report, about 18,000 people live in Winnipeg’s downtown.

More than 60,000 people work there, and some days — when there’s a big concert or the Jets play at Canada Life Centre, for example — the number of people spending time in the area increases significantly.

As Manitoba Hydro crews work to restore the last pockets of power following this week’s severe storms, some Winnipeg residents say the prolonged outages left them effectively stranded, unable to safely leave their apartments or charge essential mobility devices.

More than 30,000 Manitoba Hydro customers lost power after powerful storms swept across southern Manitoba Wednesday and Thursday, bringing down trees and power lines. Environment and Climate Change Canada recorded wind gusts of 133 km/h in Brandon, 113 km/h in Souris and 91 km/h in Winnipeg, along with more than 2,900 lightning strikes within 50 kilometres of the city.

In an update posted to social media Saturday morning, Manitoba Hydro said about 500 customers remained without power. The utility said it hoped to restore all remaining storm-related outages later in the day.

“Right now, we’re prioritizing customers that have been out the longest,” the post reads. “The final restoration work will still take time, in part because we’re dealing with small, localized outages and need to travel across a widespread area.”

MOON ALERT: Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions from 7 a.m. until 4 p.m. today. After that, the moon moves from Pisces into Aries.

ARIES (March 21-April 19)

The day is a mixed bag. There are still fun opportunities to play and enjoy socializing with others. However, you might be sandbagged by someone who is critical or negative. Be careful with whom you choose to associate, because they might irk you. Focus on home repairs.

TAURUS (April 20-May 20)

Winnipeg’s WestJet flight attendants took to the picket line outside of Richardson International Airport on the first day of nationwide strikes Sunday, while inside, frustrated flyers scrambled to re-route cancelled long-weekend flights.

The Canadian Union of Public Employees’ Ontario arm and the airline announced the strike would commence after the strike deadline was passed without a deal early Sunday morning. WestJet attendants have been without a contract since Dec. 31, 2025.

Hours later, the 240 WestJet flight attendants based in Winnipeg had walked off the job and were marching outside of the airport terminal, some carrying signs with slogans including “Tired with WestJet? So are We!” and “Unpaid Work Won’t Fly.”

Key issues causing the stalemate are wages and pay for work on the ground: the union says flight attendants are not being paid for some of that work, while the company says they pay for the work through a “credit hour” system rather than an hourly rate.

MONTREAL - Four months into the job, NDP Leader Avi Lewis is still in no rush.

Since winning the leadership of a party knocked to its knees in the 2025 federal election, Lewis has maintained his immediate priority is preparing the NDP for an election — not winning a seat in the House of Commons. Multiple byelections are set to take place before the end of the year; Lewis will be door-knocking with candidates in those ridings but won’t be on the ballot himself.

“I think there will be a point in the next year where I feel we're election-ready across the country. We want to run serious campaigns everywhere,” Lewis said in a recent interview in Montreal’s Plateau neighbourhood.

“We're in a position as a party on the rebound where I can't just pursue a seat at all costs. So I do need a litmus test for when is it time for me to get in there? And that's going be either in the next election or the run-up to the next election, once we are election-ready.”
